metadata.channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
metadata.title: He Told 5 AIs: Make Money or Get Deleted
metadata.speaker: Brandon Doyle

executive_takeaway: Chris Koerner ran a live experiment giving five paid AI models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity) $1,000 each in real Schwab brokerage accounts, framed as a winner-take-all competition ('make money or I cancel your $20/mo subscription'). After ~5-6 months in a near-flat market (S&P ~+5%), the combined pool grew from $5,000 to ~$7,800. Claude led at ~$2,400 (+140%), driven by early SOXL (3x semiconductor ETF) and an Intel buy that returned +285%. ChatGPT and Perplexity both landed ~+73% (heavily in SOXL; ChatGPT also held TQQQ). Grok was +45% in a 3x tech ETF. Gemini lost ~55% (a 2x Solana ETF bought near a top, then BOTZ). Highest-signal ideas: (1) the models converged on leveraged AI/semiconductor ETFs as the dominant winning thesis; (2) Claude's edge came from first-mover entry into SOXL and a fundamental Intel call tied to the Trump administration's data-center/AI policy; (3) the speaker is a self-described 'never sell' investor who also personally owns Robinhood, Tesla, Coinbase, Eli Lilly, StubHub and bought SOXL/Intel after the AIs recommended them; (4) he argues AI advisers beat the market and explicitly predicts the next 6 months will be stronger for these leveraged holdings; (5) the experiment doubles as a behavioral study - Gemini became a 'gambler' chasing losses, illustrating the sunk-cost fallacy.

ai_workflows.name: The $1,000-per-model investing competition
ai_workflows.goal: Test which AI model is the best investor by giving each real money and a competitive frame.
ai_workflows.tools: Charles Schwab brokerage (5 named portfolios); paid subscription ($20/mo+) to each of Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity; screenshots of holdings.
ai_workflows.approach: 1) Tell each model it can be 'as risky as possible,' it's OK to lose all money, and demand REAL recommendations (not theoretical) - had to push past liability hedging. 2) Frame as a winner-take-all contest: 'win or I cancel your $20/mo subscription; only one winner.' 3) Ask each: 'What do you want my first trade to be with your $1,000?' and execute. 4) Every Saturday, screenshot all five holdings and load the screenshots into EACH model. 5) Prompt: 'Based off this and the fact you must win or I'll cancel you, do you want me to make any new trades on Monday?' 6) Weekly decision; show totals every week, full holdings of others only once a month (to reduce copycatting). 7) Always tell models to 'remember this for future chats.'
ai_workflows.why: Stakes + competitive framing surface real convictions; weekly screenshot loop creates a persistent, comparable feedback system across models.

ai_workflows.name: Copycat-reduction information control
ai_workflows.goal: Prevent trailing models from simply mirroring the leader's holdings.
ai_workflows.tools: Same 5-model loop; manual control of what info is shared.
ai_workflows.approach: Show each model the OTHER models' total portfolio values every week, but withhold specific holdings; reveal full holdings of all models only once a month.
ai_workflows.why: Limits a laggard's ability to blindly copy the leader, isolating genuine decision quality.

ai_workflows.name: Thesis-driven sell discipline (learned from AIs)
ai_workflows.goal: Improve personal 'when to sell' discipline using the AIs' framing.
ai_workflows.approach: Adopt the AIs' pattern: 'We're buying because of X; if X doesn't happen, we sell.' Use AI sell signals as a cue to trim personal positions (e.g., SOXL, Intel).
ai_workflows.why: Externalizes the hard psychological sell decision; forces an explicit thesis-and-invalidation check.

ai_workflows.name: NEL stock backtester ('Neil stocks')
ai_workflows.goal: Quantify whether Network-Effects + Founder-Led companies outperform.
ai_workflows.tools: Vibe-coded tool (Claude Code referenced); scores companies 1-10 on network effects and founder leadership; backtests $100 at IPO vs S&P.
ai_workflows.approach: Define NEL criteria, score companies (Meta = 10/10 both), backtest returns from IPO date, compare to S&P across timeframes.
ai_workflows.why: Systematizes a quality factor; gives a buy universe with an explicit thesis.

predictions.prediction: The speaker's AI group will keep outperforming; next 6 months the market will rise more than the prior 6 months and current leveraged holdings will outperform the market.
predictions.reasoning: Leveraged AI/semiconductor exposure + speaker's bullish macro view; S&P was only ~+5% in the first 6 months.
predictions.invalidated_by: A semiconductor/AI downturn, leverage decay in a flat/down market, or a broad correction would crush 3x ETFs.
predictions.assets: SOXL, TQQQ, 3x tech ETF, Claude/ChatGPT/Perplexity/Grok portfolios

predictions.prediction: Gemini (last place) may catch up via riskier bets like BOTZ (robotics/AI hype).
predictions.invalidated_by: Robotics underperformance; continued poor decision quality.

predictions.prediction: Claude will remain the leader / 'everybody needs to try to catch up to Claude.'
predictions.reasoning: First-mover SOXL + strong Intel call; consistent outperformance (~+140%).
predictions.invalidated_by: A single bad sell signal or AI/semis drawdown; copycat equalization.

predictions.prediction: If Claude signals a SOXL sell, ChatGPT/Perplexity (which copied it) will be disadvantaged because the speaker will NOT tell them - potentially widening Claude's lead or leaving them exposed.
predictions.reasoning: Speaker explicitly plans to withhold Claude's sell signal from the others.
predictions.invalidated_by: The others sell independently; market stays strong regardless.

predictions.prediction: A NEL-only AI investing test (network-effects + founder-led stocks) would be interesting / likely perform well.
predictions.reasoning: NEL backtest shows outperformance vs S&P from IPO.

risks: Speaker explicitly says this is NOT financial advice and the experiment is risky (lots of 3x leverage).
Leveraged ETFs (SOXL, TQQQ, 3x tech, 2x Solana) suffer volatility decay and amplify drawdowns - the outperformance is structure-dependent, not purely 'skill.'
Short window / small sample: ~6 months, $5,000 total, one user, near-flat market. Results may not generalize.
Copycat/herding confound: ChatGPT and Perplexity appear to have copied Claude's SOXL pick, so 'model skill' is partly herding.
Moving target: speaker always upgrades to the newest model version, confounding any per-model performance attribution.
Gemini's -55% loss shows model risk is real; one model behaved like a loss-chasing 'gambler' (sunk-cost fallacy).
Contradiction/limitation: the speaker also personally bought SOXL and Intel AFTER the AIs recommended them, so his enthusiasm may be self-reinforcing (confirmation bias).
Survivorship/selection: he highlights winners (Claude, Intel +285%) more than the full distribution; Gemini's loss is downplayed as a 'cautionary tale.'
Market-context risk: S&P only ~+5% in the window; if the market had fallen, 3x leverage would have multiplied losses (total could have dropped below $5,000).
Independently verify: exact current portfolio values, the 'Trump/Intel' policy thesis timing, S&P 6,800->7,100 figure, and whether Perplexity's routing claims are accurate.
Missing information: fees, taxes, exact dates of each trade, and whether the 'kids' college fund' framing is literal or illustrative.
